extracted.intended_audience: Participants and principals in FCC covered transactions (e.g., service providers, Lifeline/ACP providers, USF/TRS/NDBEDP participants), lower-tier contractors/marketing organizations, and FCC officials/SDOs
extracted.subtask_short: FCC nonprocurement suspension and debarment rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards for nonprocurement suspension, debarment, disclosures, exceptions, and related reporting/recordkeeping applicable to participants in FCC-covered programs (USF, TRS, NDBEDP, Lifeline/ACP, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB Guidelines as Commission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts the Guidelines in part 180, subparts A through I of this title, as supplemented by this part, as Commission policies, procedures, and requirements for nonprocurement debarment and suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All persons affected should consult part 180, subparts A–I to be informed of all provisions of the suspension and debarment rules. For any section of part 180 without a corresponding section in this part, Commission policies and procedures are those in the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to: (a) 'Participant' or 'principal' in a covered transaction under part 180 as supplemented by this part; (b) respondents in Commission suspension or debarment actions; (c) Commission SDOs; and (d) Commission officials or agents authorized to enter into covered nonprocurement transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult §6001.110 for the full list of who is covered; persons should also consult the referenced portions of part 180.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory advance disclosures for all participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must make advance disclosures prior to entering into covered transactions that include: (1) notification whether any principals have been convicted, indicted, or civilly charged by any government entity for certain offenses during the past three years; (2) notification whether participants are excluded or disqualified from covered transactions; and (3) notification to the Commission if an entity is excluded by another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures are mandatory for all participants in covered Commission programs and are intended to allow Commission scrutiny to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional mandatory disclosures for lower tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower tier participants must: (1) notify the higher tier participant of the information described in 2 CFR 180.335; (2) notify the higher tier participant if participating in competitive bidding at time of the bid; (3) notify the USF, TRS, NDBEDP, and ACP Administrators if participating in transactions related to those programs; (4) notify the FCC; and (5) notify those entities if the lower tier participant learns of new information required under 2 CFR 180.335.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additional disclosures ensure higher-tier participants and program administrators are aware of potential risks arising from lower-tier participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary-tier confirmation obligations before entering a transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary tier participants must confirm that those with whom they do business are not excluded or disqualified from government activities, which can be accomplished by checking SAM.gov Exclusions, by a certification, or by adding terms to the applicable transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary participants must also communicate requirements to lower tier participants by collecting certifications or including transaction terms requiring compliance with subpart C of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding and hiring certification requirements for Lifeline/ACP providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Service providers must certify that they have processes requiring employees (and contractors/independent contractors) of their own organizations and of their marketing organizations/contractors/subcontractors to disclose whether they are suspended or debarred or have been required to resign due to malfeasance within the past three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification should confirm that impacted companies will not hire individuals disclosing suspension/debarment or such resignations/terminations, and that neither the service providers nor their contractors/subcontractors shall enter into business relationships with suspended or debarred companies/individuals or those who disclosed such exclusions or resignations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document retention substantiating certifications (Lifeline and ACP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary participants in Lifeline must maintain documents substantiating their required certification for the three full years preceding; ACP primary tier participants must maintain such documentation for the six full preceding calendar years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents must be provided to the Commission or USAC upon request to substantiate certification claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual disclosure filing for Lifeline and ACP primary tier participants
rubrics_metrics.description: ETCs who are primary tier participants and their lower tier participants in the Lifeline program are required to file annual disclosure statements, under penalty of perjury, reporting all required disclosures or certifying that they have no reportable disclosures. ACP primary tier participants have the same disclosure requirements (with six-year documentation retention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary participants may file on behalf of lower tier participants with which they have a direct relationship and must maintain substantiating documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: USF competitive-bidding short-form vs long-form disclosure regime
rubrics_metrics.description: At the short-form application stage of USF auctions, applicants are required only to disclose whether the applicant or any of its principals are presently excluded or disqualified from any Federal government programs. Only applicants that become winning bidders and proceed to the long-form stage must provide all disclosures mandated by the OMB Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form minimizes initial burdens; full vetting occurs at long-form stage for winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRS and NDBEDP program-specific disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: TRS or NDBEDP certification applicants must file required disclosures as part of certification and renewal; internet-based TRS providers must update disclosures within 60 days of any change by filing a Notice of Substantive Change; NDBEDP providers must update disclosures with six-month program reports and file a change as a notification of substantive change if it bears directly on qualification for certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These program-specific timing rules ensure up-to-date disclosure information for program administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person excluded by Commission action or another agency is not already registered with SAM.gov, that person must register within 10 days after the suspension or debarment becomes effective. Persons already listed in SAM.gov Exclusions when this part takes effect must provide notice of such exclusion to the Commission within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be emailed and mailed to the Chief of the responsible Bureau(s), the Administrators of any such program, the General Counsel, and the Office of the Managing Director. For exclusions occurring after the part's effective date, notice must be provided within 10 days after receiving notice of the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on entering new covered transactions while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded persons may temporarily continue with existing covered transactions but may not enter into any new covered transactions or provide services for such transactions unless an exception is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded persons must comply with orders for transitions or limited continuations as required by the SDO; excluded persons shall be immediately barred from enrolling new customers or entering new covered transactions upon notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial suspension vs final suspension operational effects
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial suspension decision prevents the suspended party from enrolling new customers or otherwise entering into new covered transactions but an initial suspension made before an opportunity to oppose shall not trigger discontinuation of service or require beneficiaries to find alternative providers until a final suspension decision is reached or the time to contest has passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discontinuations or substitution requirements are not effective until final suspension procedures are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO authority and exclusivity over exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delegates exclusive authority to its SDO in the first instance to grant exceptions to exclusions. Neither the Commission nor the Chairperson will rule on exceptions in the first instance, although the Commission may consider applications for review of an SDO decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions, if granted, must be in writing and state reasons for deviating from governmentwide policy, and may be subject to conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and factors SDO shall consider when evaluating exception requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating requests for exceptions the SDO shall evaluate the particular services provided by the excluded person, availability of alternate providers in the areas served, typical contract terms between provider and beneficiaries, any applicable federal/state certification requirements (especially for NDBEDP or TRS), when the misconduct occurred, and, for exclusions by other agencies, when the exclusion was issued and how much longer it will remain in effect. The SDO may consider any other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO shall balance the goal of providing continued services to beneficiaries with protecting program integrity, consult with program bureaus/offices and the Office of General Counsel, and issue a written ruling on the exception request. Exceptions may include conditions like mandatory audits, additional reporting, compliance agreements, monitoring, or other oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDO preliminary evaluation upon notice of another-agency exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of an exclusion issued by another agency, and upon request by participants or an FCC bureau/office, the SDO shall preliminarily evaluate whether to grant an exception after consulting OGC and bureaus, considering factors including when the misconduct occurred, when the other agency issued the exclusion, how much longer the exclusion will remain in effect, and availability of alternate providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the SDO preliminarily determines no exception is warranted, it will promptly initiate informal proceedings on transitions to alternate providers or limited continuations with notice to the excluded person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timeline for excluded person's response
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice initiating transition/continuation proceedings, excluded persons shall have 30 days to file responses to the notice and may seek an exception by stating in writing the reasons for such an exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the proceedings, the SDO will issue a decision ruling on any exception request and setting appropriate transition or continuation requirements if the exception is denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose conditions when granting exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any exceptions granted by the SDO may be subject to appropriate conditions such as mandatory audits, additional reporting requirements, compliance agreements (with OGC approval), monitoring, or other forms of effective oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions are intended to ensure that an excluded person granted an exception complies with Commission program requirements and protects program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/transition flexibility and case‑by‑case review
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB Guidelines and FCC supplemental rules allow case-by-case review to prevent penalizing entities (e.g., schools/libraries) for the misconduct of a lower tier participant, and permit limited continuation with an excluded provider in existing transactions until a substitute provider can be found or for a reasonable transition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO will evaluate factors such as availability of alternate providers and the Commission's goals of preventing waste, fraud, and abuse to determine whether to grant exceptions for continuations or transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower tier passing-down methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary participants must use methods such as collecting certifications or including transaction terms/conditions to pass suspension/debarment and disclosure requirements down to lower tier participants with whom they intend to do business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §6001.330 for required methods and §6001.335 for additional information disclosures for primary and lower tier participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of unfavorable disclosures by Bureaus and Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureaus and Administrators are to review unfavorable disclosures by participants and may consider mitigating factors when assessing the impact of unfavorable disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SDO has flexibility to evaluate actions of a lower tier participant along with mitigating factors, allowing tailoring of impacts on primary tier participants; unfavorable disclosures are unlikely to be outcome determinative except where facts require exclusion to protect programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered transaction threshold remains $25,000
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission maintains the $25,000 contract valuation threshold (as included in the OMB Guidelines) that defines a 'covered transaction' and triggers lower tier participant obligations; the Commission declines to raise the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A higher threshold could interfere with governmentwide reciprocity for excluded entities; the SDO may consider actual or potential harm (including dollar value) as a mitigating factor in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Commission exclusion and governmentwide reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person suspended or debarred by a Commission order is excluded from participation in any Commission program and will be placed on SAM.gov Exclusions, triggering reciprocity barring that person from participating in other government programs unless granted an exemption by another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exclusion by the Commission has broad cross‑program consequences; exceptions do not extend to covered transactions of another agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded definition of 'principal'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this part, 'principal' includes consultants that have a business relationship with any participant in connection with a covered transaction and Lifeline or ACP marketing organizations, and any other person having critical influence on, or substantive control over, a covered transaction. An individual's status as a principal does not depend on employment or payment with federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expanded definition broadens who must be considered when making disclosures and assessing exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, recordkeeping, and compliance obligations for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small and other entities participating in covered Commission programs will have new reporting, recordkeeping, and other compliance obligations consistent with the OMB Guidelines and FCC supplemental rules; the Commission cannot quantify compliance costs but expects entities to leverage existing compliance mechanisms used for other government programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFA requires description of economic impacts and projected reporting/recordkeeping; small entities should be aware of additional administrative obligations and possible need to maintain or adapt compliance processes.
